chunks: Al-Hasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام came out of the bathhouse.
A man said to him, “May your bathing be pleasant.” He said to him, “O fool, what are you doing with mentioning the backside here?”
So he said, “May your bathhouse be pleasant.” He said, “If the bathhouse is pleasant, then what comfort is there for the body from it?”
He said, “May your hot water be pleasant.” He said, “Woe to you! Do you not know that al-ḥamīm is sweat?”
He said to him, “How should I speak?” He said, “Say: May what has been purified from you be pleasant, and purified be what is pleasant from you.”

key_terms.اسْتِحْمَامُكَ: your bathing or use of the bath
key_terms.لُكَعُ: a rebuke meaning fool or ignorant person

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Hasan عليه السلام teach proper etiquette and wording when speaking about bathing and cleanliness?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts how Imam al-Hasan عليه السلام corrected a man’s expressions after leaving the bathhouse, teaching him to use proper and refined speech. It highlights etiquette, linguistic precision, and the preference for expressions that convey cleanliness and purity in a dignified manner.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.297 - Imam Hasan ibn Ali (as) came out of the bathhouse
, and a man met him and said:
"May your (backside) bathing be good."
Imam (as) said: "O’ fool, what business do you have mentioning the ‘backside’ here ?"
(The man) replied: "May your bath be pleasant"
Imam (as) said: "And if my bath is pleasant, what benefit is that to me?"
(The man) replied: "May your warm water be pleasant."
Imam (as) said: "Woe to you! Do you not know that 'Hamim' (hot water) is sweat?"
(The man) asked Him: “So what should I say?”
Imam (as) said: "Say: 'May what is purified from you be pleasant, and may what is pleasant from you be purified.'".
